solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Light colour in room without central heating initially

indicators.note: without means the following letters are taken away from the room word

parts.note: a chamber is a room

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A cold, dimly lit room with no central heating switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes C and H, the first letters of 'central heating'; 'without' removes them from CHAMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a yellowish-orange shade, and also the middle traffic light.

clue.text: Be sore, husband being trapped by expert

indicators.note: being trapped by means the husband letter sits inside the expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A sore husband caught out by a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to hurt dully, a verb synonym for being sore.

clue.text: City in which one will get wet

definitions.meaning: an English spa city in Somerset

definitions.text: in which one will get wet

explanation.surface: A rainy city where visitors are sure to get soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in Somerset is famous for Roman spas; the same word names a tub you wash in.

clue.text: Salesman going over border with carpet

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
a rim is a border or edge
and means together with

explanation.surface: A sales rep crossing a boundary with a rug for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is the verb: to carpet someone is British slang for scolding them.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is a British idiom for a formal telling-off, so a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tramps getting something to eat in pubs

indicators.note: in places the food inside the word for pubs

parts.note: bars are pubs
an egg is something to eat

explanation.surface: Vagrants getting a meal in drinking establishments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps are homeless people who may live by begging, so a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Bishop with books on some plants in this study

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
OT, the Old Testament, is a set of books
any means some

explanation.surface: A bishop with books studying some plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany is the scientific study of plant life, so a definition by description.

clue.text: Young girl's love missed in jail

indicators.note: missed means the zero letter is left out

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A young woman's lover absent because he is in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Fish. of course, coming from south island

parts.note: to angle is to fish

indicators.note: coming from south means in this down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: yes, of course, an affirmative

explanation.surface: Fishing, naturally, off an island to the south.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, reading 'from south' means bottom to top, so YES becomes SEY. Anglesey is an island off north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglesey is a large Welsh island in the Irish Sea, an example of an island.

clue.text: Save time when in grip of terrible disease

indicators.note: when in grip of means the time letter is held inside
terrible means the letters of disease are mangled

explanation.surface: Saving time while in the clutches of an awful illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DISEASE into SEASIDE; 'when in grip of' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside money is to save or reserve it, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Dangerous place, where stolen drug is cut by dealers finally

indicators.note: is cut by means a letter splits the stolen-drug phrase open

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
pot is slang for cannabis

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of dealers

explanation.surface: A risky spot where stolen narcotics are adulterated by pushers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cut by' sounds like drug-dealing jargon for adulterating, but it puts S (from 'finally') inside HOTPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouble spot or area of danger or conflict is called this, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Fair match, perhaps

definitions.meaning: fair as in pale-coloured, not dark
a match is one example of something used to give a flame

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture that is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means pale in colour, and a match is something you strike as a source of flame.

clue.text: People sleeping outside and flipping criminals

indicators.note: outside means the sleepers go around the other piece

parts.note: kippers are people having a kip, a British word for sleep

indicators.note: flipping means the word and is turned round

explanation.surface: Sleepers outdoors and some furious lawbreakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads like a mild British swear word qualifying criminals, but it is the reversal signal; 'kip' is British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnappers are a kind of criminal: those who abduct people for ransom.

clue.text: Fruit in pie pen pal's written about

indicators.note: written about means the letters of the pie, pen and pal words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tropical fruit mentioned in a letter from a pen friend about pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A pineapple is a tropical fruit, an example of the category.

clue.text: Front of vehicle seen on screen

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
to screen is to guard or shield

explanation.surface: The front of a car showing up on a television screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The vanguard is the leading part of an army or movement, its front.

clue.text: Force Alf when drunk to go way

indicators.note: when drunk means the letters of force alf are scrambled

explanation.surface: Making a drunken man named Alf leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear off is an informal command meaning leave or depart, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: A change for shopkeepers on board

parts.note: a float is the cash a shop keeps in the till to give change

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's store of coins kept on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on board a vessel at sea means being carried on water, the adverbial sense.

clue.text: Really popular act

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a stage turn is truly well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are emphatic adverbs expressing truth or surprise, so synonyms.

clue.text: Queen's partner maybe caught tucking into most of the red fruit?

indicators.note: tucking into means the caught letter goes inside the shortened fruit
most of means the final letter of the fruit is dropped

parts.note: a tomato is a red fruit
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The monarch's consort eating most of a tomato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' here is a female cat, not royalty; 'most of' trims TOMATO to TOMAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female cat, so her mate may be a male cat.

clue.text: Glad to rant wildly, seeing final amount

indicators.note: wildly means the letters of glad to rant are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone happy to complain furiously on seeing the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The sum reached at the end of adding everything up, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Joke involving judge and parrot

parts.note: to parrot is to ape or mimic

explanation.surface: A prank involving a judge and a pet bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a practical joke or prank, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Just about? Extremely likely!

parts.note: on means about, concerning

indicators.note: extremely means take the outer letters of likely

explanation.surface: A doubtful question answered with a confident affirmation.
explanation.definitionFit: Only and just are adverbs both meaning merely or no more than.

clue.text: Duck keen to eat duck!

indicators.note: to eat means one word swallows the other

parts.note: avid means keen
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: An eager duck gobbling up another duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Duck' is the verb to dodge; the second is the cricket zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge or evade it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fellow's almost finished

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: done means finished

explanation.surface: A man nearly done with his work.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university fellow or tutor, especially at Oxford or Cambridge.

clue.text: Officer having better army home

parts.note: to cap is to better or top something
TA is the Territorial Army, the UK reserve force
in means at home

explanation.surface: A military officer with a superior army residence.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a rank of commissioned officer in the army or navy.

clue.text: No longer used in part of nationwide functions

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something obsolete among events held across the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defunct has ceased to exist or operate, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Funeral poem, say, written in cathedral city

indicators.note: written in means the example abbreviation sits inside the city

parts.note: Ely is a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A mourning verse composed in a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a lament for the dead, a mournful poem often read at funerals.
